title: Avalanche Risk Intelligence Portal
tagline: A decision-support portal for avalanche situational awareness in northern Pakistan.
summary: A Flask-based portal for the Hindu Kush, Karakoram and Western Himalaya: 15-day season windows, an interactive map, study-area filtering, settlement and road exposure analysis, CSV/GeoJSON exports with provenance, and a drop-in slot for machine-learning predictions. Built for NDMA's Next Generation Technologies programme as decision support, not official warnings.
problem: Avalanche risk depends on many interacting factors: slope angle, aspect, elevation, recent snowfall, wind loading and temperature. That information is spread across terrain models, satellite imagery and weather feeds in different formats and resolutions, which makes it hard to bring together into one clear, location-specific picture of where terrain is most susceptible.
solution: A Python data pipeline that ingests a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and satellite data, derives terrain features such as slope, aspect and curvature, and combines them with weather variables. Supervised machine learning models (Random Forest and Support Vector Machine) are trained to classify terrain susceptibility, and the results are rendered as layers on an interactive web map so they can be explored visually.

architecture.overview: A Flask application with a small service layer and a dataset registry. Heavy geospatial work happens offline; the web layer serves filtered data, exports and a printable brief. Model outputs drop into a folder per 15-day window.

layers.name: Data registry
items: catalog.json: source, date, CRS, resolution, limitations per dataset

layers.name: Services
items: Spatial maths: haversine, point-in-polygon, line distance

layers.name: Model slot
items: Random Forest / SVM terrain classifiers (in development)

features.title: Terrain feature extraction
features.description: Derives slope angle, aspect and curvature from elevation data, which are the core terrain variables used in avalanche assessment.

features.title: Satellite data integration
features.description: Brings satellite-derived information into the same spatial grid as the terrain model so every location has a consistent set of features.

features.title: ML susceptibility classification
features.description: Trains and compares Random Forest and SVM models to classify terrain into susceptibility categories.

features.title: Interactive risk map
features.description: Displays model output as toggleable map layers with a clear legend, so results can be explored by location.

challenges.title: Never faking data
challenges.description: Hazard zones and model output aren't available yet. The portal shows 'No data' or 'Not assessed' instead of filling gaps with synthetic values, and every dataset carries its limitations.

challenges.title: Aligning heterogeneous sources
challenges.description: Settlements, incidents, roads and extents come with different accuracy and provenance. A catalog with CRS, resolution and date keeps them honest.

challenges.title: Decision support, not warnings
challenges.description: Outputs are framed as situational awareness; official warnings remain with NDMA/PDMA. The interface says so everywhere.

learnings: Working with raster geospatial data, coordinate reference systems and reprojection
Choosing evaluation metrics suited to imbalanced classification
Designing pipelines that separate heavy offline processing from a fast web layer
whoItHelps: Disaster-management teams, district authorities and researchers who need one clear, location-specific picture of avalanche exposure during the winter season.
currentStatus: Portal, data registry, exposure analysis, exports and tests are built (15 automated tests). Hazard/runout layers and the prediction model are not yet connected; the portal shows 'No data' rather than synthetic values until they are.

title: AI Business Automation Agent
tagline: An AI agent that runs business workflows, connects APIs, processes information, and produces structured reports.
summary: An AI agent architecture that takes routine business tasks, such as gathering data from connected services, processing it and producing structured reports, and automates them end to end with logging and human review.
highlights: Every step logged for human review
Live demo API on this site
problem: Small teams spend significant time on repetitive operational work: copying data between tools, compiling status updates, summarising information and preparing recurring reports. The work is necessary but low-leverage, and doing it by hand is slow and error-prone.
solution: An agent built around a large language model that can plan a task, call a defined set of tools (API integrations, data processing functions, report generators) and assemble the results. Workflows are triggered on a schedule or by events, every step is logged, and outputs can be held for human review before they are sent.

architecture.overview: A Python service hosts the agent loop. The LLM decides which tool to call next; each tool is a small, tested Python function with a strict input schema. A workflow layer handles triggers, retries and logging.

features.title: Tool-calling agent
features.description: The LLM selects from a defined set of tools with validated inputs instead of producing free-form actions.

features.title: API integrations
features.description: Connectors for external services let the agent read and write data where the business already works.

features.title: Intelligent reporting
features.description: Collected data is summarised into structured, readable reports generated automatically.

features.title: Logging & human review
features.description: Every run is logged step by step, and sensitive outputs can require approval before they are sent.

challenges.title: Reliability of LLM output
challenges.description: LLMs can produce inconsistent output. Strict tool schemas, validation and retries are needed to keep the workflow predictable.

challenges.title: Safe tool access
challenges.description: An agent should only have the permissions a task requires. Scoping credentials and actions is part of the design.

challenges.title: Cost and latency
challenges.description: Each model call costs time and money, so workflows have to be designed to use the model only where it adds value.

learnings: Designing tool interfaces that LLMs can use reliably
Building observable automation with logs and review steps
Integrating multiple third-party APIs behind a consistent internal interface
whoItHelps: Small teams spending hours on inbox triage, data entry between tools and recurring reports.
currentStatus: Prototype with a working rule-based engine and live demo API on this site; LLM planning layer planned.
thumbnailAlt: The AI Business Automation Agent's 3D workflow exhibit with its status, log and engine panels

title: AI-Enabled Car Sales Platform
tagline: A full-stack dealership platform with lead management and business automation.
summary: A full-stack web application for a car sales business: vehicle listings, customer inquiries captured as leads, a lead management dashboard and automation that helps the sales team respond faster.
highlights: Lead scoring and pipeline demo (live on this site)
problem: Smaller car dealerships often manage inventory and customer inquiries across spreadsheets, phone calls and messaging apps. Leads get lost, follow-ups are inconsistent and there is little visibility into where each potential buyer is in the sales process.
solution: A Flask web application with a public vehicle catalogue and inquiry forms that feed directly into a lead management system. Staff get a dashboard to track lead status, and automation handles repetitive steps such as lead notifications, follow-up reminders and AI-assisted inquiry summaries.

architecture.overview: A server-rendered Flask application backed by a relational database, with background automation jobs and optional AI services for working with inquiry text.

features.title: Vehicle catalogue
features.description: Searchable listings with detail pages so customers can browse available inventory.

features.title: Lead capture
features.description: Inquiry and test-drive forms create structured lead records automatically instead of scattered messages.

features.title: Lead management dashboard
features.description: Staff can see every lead, its status and its history in one place.

features.title: Sales automation
features.description: Automatic notifications and follow-up reminders reduce the chance of a lead being forgotten.

challenges.title: Modelling the sales pipeline
challenges.description: Lead stages and status transitions need to match how a dealership actually works, which shapes the data model.

challenges.title: Useful, not intrusive, automation
challenges.description: Reminders and notifications should help staff without creating noise or spamming customers.

challenges.title: Data quality
challenges.description: Form validation and duplicate handling keep the lead database clean and trustworthy.

learnings: Structuring a Flask application with clear separation of routes, models and services
Designing relational data models for a real business process
Applying automation to a concrete sales workflow
whoItHelps: Smaller dealerships managing inventory and leads across spreadsheets and messaging apps.
currentStatus: In development; lead scoring and pipeline demo are live on this site.

title: Batura Glacier Satellite-Imagery CNN Analysis
tagline: Sentinel-2 time series of Batura Glacier (2020–2026) from Google Earth Engine, prepared for CNN analysis.
summary: A Python pipeline that builds half-month Sentinel-2 median composites of Batura Glacier (Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan) in Google Earth Engine, exports them as GeoTIFFs and CNN-ready NumPy tile arrays, and checks every image for gaps and cloud. The CNN analysis of glacier change over 2020–2026 is in progress.
whoItHelps: Glaciologists, climate researchers and water-resource planners who need a consistent, reproducible satellite record of a glacier rather than one-off downloads.
currentStatus: Pipeline, quality checks and the CNN dataset loader are built. Composites are being generated back to 2020. The CNN change-analysis models are in development.
problem: Studying a glacier over years means hundreds of satellite scenes with clouds, gaps and inconsistent processing. Downloading them by hand is slow and the results are not reproducible, which makes any model trained on them hard to trust.
solution: An Earth Engine pipeline produces one cloud-filtered median composite per half-month, saves GeoTIFFs plus 256×256 tile arrays scaled for neural networks, writes previews and contact sheets for visual cloud checks, and logs every image. Runs are resumable and only build what is missing.

architecture.overview: Batch processing in Google Earth Engine, exported to Google Drive, with local verification and a dataset loader for PyTorch.

layers.name: Acquisition
items: Automatic window widening when scenes are missing

layers.name: Quality
items: Per-image run log and quality report
RGB previews and yearly contact sheets

layers.name: Analysis
items: CNN models for glacier change (in development)

features.title: Reproducible composites
features.description: Every half-month from 2020 to 2026 is built the same way, so comparisons across years are fair.

features.title: CNN-ready output
features.description: Tiles are pre-scaled and gridded with a loader that gives per-tile time series straight to PyTorch.

features.title: Built-in quality checks
features.description: A verification pass lists missing, broken, cloudy or widened images and renders contact sheets to eyeball.

features.title: Resumable runs
features.description: Stop any time; finished images are skipped and half-written files never appear under their final name.

challenges.title: Clouds and gaps
challenges.description: Mountain weather leaves many half-months with few clear scenes. The pipeline widens the window and records that it did, rather than hiding it.

challenges.title: Data volume
challenges.description: Years of 10 m imagery add up. Tiled, compressed GeoTIFFs and memory-mapped arrays keep it workable on a laptop.

challenges.title: Honest modelling
challenges.description: Glacier change is subtle; model claims will only be made after proper validation against known reference data.

learnings: Earth Engine batch processing and export limits

title: Wind & Solar Energy Potential Prediction
tagline: Machine learning that predicts wind and solar energy potential in coastal areas.
summary: A machine-learning project that predicts wind and solar energy potential for coastal locations from weather and environmental data, related to my co-authored IEEE conference paper on ML-based energy prediction for hybrid solar-wind energy harvesters.
whoItHelps: Renewable-energy planners and engineers deciding where hybrid solar-wind systems are worth installing.
currentStatus: Research prototype. Models and evaluation exist as project work; a public repository and write-up are planned.
problem: Hybrid solar-wind systems only pay off where both resources are reliable. Measuring that on site for every candidate location is slow and expensive, and simple averages miss how the two resources vary together.
solution: Supervised machine-learning models trained on historical weather and environmental variables estimate wind and solar energy potential per location, so promising coastal sites can be ranked before field measurement.

architecture.overview: A classical ML workflow: data collection, feature engineering, model training and comparison, and evaluation with held-out data.

features.title: Site ranking
features.description: Estimates energy potential per location so sites can be compared before investment.

features.title: Hybrid view
features.description: Treats wind and solar together, which matters for hybrid harvesters.

features.title: Transparent evaluation
features.description: Reports errors on unseen data instead of training-set scores.

challenges.title: Data availability
challenges.description: Coastal measurement data is sparse; the quality of public weather data limits what the models can learn.

challenges.title: Generalisation
challenges.description: A model that fits one coastline may not transfer; evaluation by location guards against that.

learnings: Feature engineering for environmental time series
Writing up ML results for peer review

title: Final-Year Project: Computer Vision with CNNs
tagline: Deep-learning computer vision with convolutional neural networks (NUST Mechatronics, 2026).
summary: My NUST final-year project applies convolutional neural networks to a computer-vision task, covering dataset preparation, model training, evaluation and deployment considerations for a real system.
whoItHelps: Teams that need images automatically understood: inspection, monitoring or detection tasks where manual review doesn't scale.
currentStatus: Final-year project in progress (2026). Details of the task, dataset and results will be published here once the work is complete.
problem: Many real-world monitoring tasks depend on people looking at images. That is slow, inconsistent and hard to scale.
solution: Convolutional neural networks trained on a prepared dataset, with careful validation, to automate the visual task end to end.

architecture.overview: A standard deep-learning pipeline from data to a deployable model.

features.title: End-to-end pipeline
features.description: From raw images to a trained, evaluated model.

features.title: Mechatronics integration
features.description: Designed with the hardware and control side of a real system in mind.

challenges.title: Data quality
challenges.description: Model quality is bounded by labelling quality; the pipeline invests in clean splits and augmentation.

challenges.title: Honest reporting
challenges.description: Results will be published with their validation method, not headline numbers alone.

learnings: Bridging ML models and physical systems
